name: KIP Standard Memory Policy
description: The standard deterministic Projection Policy for memory recall (Spec §21.13): the structural baseline plus three ordered precedence rules — context specificity, first-person testimony, recency. No numeric weighting.

time.missing_valid_time: from: the bound {latest: asserted_at} — the value began no later than the claim (Spec §25.2); until: open (ends at a successor, Spec §25.4)
time.succession: same_actor_same_context_lines for Assertions that take part: mode stated or observed, or a written from (Spec §25.4)

assertion_lifecycle.note: expired is computed from world time (Spec §14.3), never a stored status: an Assertion outside its effective interval at valid_at contributes nothing.

confidence.note: Assertion confidence is preserved/reported but does not decide fixture status.

trust.note: The standard memory policy weighs no trust; trust-weighted policies are weighted_projection (Spec §67.4).

belief_slot.functional_predicate_rule: If two or more distinct candidate objects each have accepted/strong support and their valid-time intervals overlap for a functional Predicate, the slot status is contested.

leading.note: Disclosure only: leading never changes status (Spec §21.6, §27.2).

projection.final_conflict_rule: Compute candidate status first, then mark every materially supported member of an unresolved functional/exclusive conflict contested, including grounded BELIEF and BELIEF-by-id. accepted_values contains only final accepted candidates.
projection.dependency_validity: An inferred derivation with needs_review/unverifiable basis cannot be final accepted; report uncertain unless contested or rejected is already warranted.

canonicalization.description: RFC 8785 JCS, narrowed to KIP portable safe integral values; no nonzero underflow; strict decoded-key/Unicode validation; integrity excluded from its own digest.

precedence.applies_to: conflict sets of a functional slot or functional_by partition at the basis

rules.context_specificity: candidate A prevails over B when some eligible support of A has a context set that strictly contains the context set of every eligible support of B
rules.first_person_testimony: candidate A prevails over B when A has eligible support stated or observed by the slot's subject and no eligible support of B is by the subject or has mode observed
rules.recency: candidate A prevails over B when the greatest start key (Spec §25.4: exact from, else the bound's latest, else asserted_at) among A's eligible support is greater than the greatest start key among B's eligible support; equal keys do not decide

precedence.decision: the first rule under which one candidate prevails over every other decides; otherwise the conflict stands
